# Workspace releases

The root `pi-roundtable` package and every `packages/*` workspace share one version.
A single `v<version>` tag runs `publish.yml`: the existing core job checks the entire tree and publishes the core, then a matrix publishes each workspace independently.
The matrix is generated by `scripts/check-release.ts`, so adding `sandbox` or `mcp` needs no new publishing job.
The root's `files` allowlist does not include `packages/`.

## Development

Run `bun install --frozen-lockfile` at the repository root.
After changing workspace manifests, remove root and workspace `node_modules` before installing: Bun 1.4.2's incremental relinking can leave child-local core links pointing at the child itself.
The workspace linkage regression test fails on such stale links.
If they persist after a clean install, rebuild `bun.lock` from scratch with Bun 1.4.2 and review the newly resolved dependencies: its older lockfile format can retain invalid nested root entries.
The committed lockfile uses the current format; clean installation and repeated frozen installation both pass the linkage regression.
Bun does not treat the root package as a child workspace; the root-only `pi-roundtable: link:.` override and hoisted linker give every workspace a live symlink to the core.
Workspace manifests use ordinary semver for both the core development dependency and its peer range.
No workspace or local-path dependency specifier is shipped in a workspace manifest.
A consuming project ignores the root package's development override.

Run core checks with `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`, and `bun run test`.
Run all workspace checks with `bun run check:packages`.
Run `bun run --cwd packages/web build` to build the console assets.
CI performs these checks with PostgreSQL and native canvas prerequisites installed.

## First publication and trust

These are owner actions, not part of the migration.
Use Node 24 and npm 11.15 or newer, enable account 2FA, and log in with browser/security-key authentication using `npm login`.
Core `0.7.0` and its original `v0.7.0` tag already exist; this migration leaves that release commit unchanged.
Check the migration commit's CI before publishing the new packages.
From the repository root, install and run the checks above, then publish each new package manually:

```sh
(cd packages/drawing && npm publish --access public --provenance=false)
(cd packages/coding && npm publish --access public --provenance=false)
(cd packages/web && npm publish --access public --provenance=false)
```

The web package's `prepack` builds `dist/` automatically.
Local publication disables provenance because provenance is generated by supported CI environments, not a developer's shell.
Each package must exist on npm before trusted publishing can be configured.
Configure every package against the same workflow file:

```sh
npm trust github pi-roundtable-drawing --file publish.yml --repo wayne930242/pi-roundtable --allow-publish
npm trust github pi-roundtable-coding --file publish.yml --repo wayne930242/pi-roundtable --allow-publish
npm trust github pi-roundtable-web --file publish.yml --repo wayne930242/pi-roundtable --allow-publish
```

The core's existing trust stays on `publish.yml`.
No package-specific tags or workflows are used.

## Subsequent lockstep releases

Update the root version and every workspace version together.
Update every workspace's core development dependency to that version and its peer range to the matching minor, for example `>=0.8.0 <0.9.0` for `0.8.0`.
Update changelogs, regenerate `bun.lock`, and run the clean-install checks and packing checks.
Run `bun scripts/check-release.ts v0.8.0` before committing: it refuses mismatched versions, core peer ranges, development pins, and repository directories.
Run `bun scripts/preflight-release.ts v0.8.0`: it packs every workspace, checks required files (including the web HTML/JS/CSS and drawing fonts), and requires each package to exist on npm before the core can publish.
Use `--local` only for CI or pre-first-publish checks, where a new package need not yet exist on npm.
Verify every workspace's trusted publisher is configured against this repository's `publish.yml` before pushing a release tag; package existence alone does not prove OIDC authorization.
Commit and push, wait for CI for that exact commit, then have the owner push the single `v0.8.0` tag.
`publish.yml` checks all versions before any publication and publishes all packages with provenance through npm OIDC.
If a package job fails after other packages publish, rerun only the failed jobs rather than republishing the successful core or packages.
Do not use Re-run all jobs: npm refuses to overwrite the already-published core version, stopping the downstream matrix.
Publication across multiple npm packages is not atomic; pack/existence preflight cannot guarantee registry availability or OIDC authorization.

## Importing sandbox later

Do not import a repository while its writer is still working.
Once its final commit is known and the source and destination tracked trees are clean, run at the root:

```sh
git subtree add --prefix=packages/sandbox ../pi-roundtable-sandbox master
```

Keep the full history; do not add `--squash`.
Remove `packages/sandbox/bun.lock` and the imported `packages/sandbox/.github/workflows/ci.yml` and `publish.yml`.
Set its own version and core development dependency to the root version, currently `0.7.0`, and its core peer range to `>=0.7.0 <0.8.0`.
Set its repository URL to `git+https://github.com/wayne930242/pi-roundtable.git` and directory to `packages/sandbox`.
Set its Biome config's `root` to `false`, retain its package-specific rules, and expose `typecheck`, `lint`, and `test` scripts.
Keep shared Pi dependencies on compatible ranges, not exact pins, so the canary and consuming hosts can deduplicate the core's Pi instances.
Add only its public metadata paths to the scanner's name allowlist and add its README link near the official packages in `docs/plugins.md`.
Remove all installed root/workspace `node_modules`, run `bun install`, and exercise core checks, `check:packages`, the public scan, `check-release.ts`, and every package's `npm pack --dry-run` and packed manifest.
Verify the core's pack file list is unchanged, then commit, push, and check that commit's CI.
The workspace glob and publish matrix automatically include sandbox.
Its owner-only first publication and trust commands are:

```sh
(cd packages/sandbox && npm publish --access public --provenance=false)
npm trust github pi-roundtable-sandbox --file publish.yml --repo wayne930242/pi-roundtable --allow-publish
```

## Moving the already-published MCP package

Apply the same import procedure with `packages/mcp` and its actual source branch after this migration.
Its package version jumps from `0.4.1` to the lockstep version; set the core peer range and repository directory accordingly.
It needs no manual first publication because it already exists on npm.
The owner must move its trust away from the old repository before the next lockstep tag:

```sh
npm trust list pi-roundtable-mcp
npm trust revoke pi-roundtable-mcp --id <old-trust-id>
npm trust github pi-roundtable-mcp --file publish.yml --repo wayne930242/pi-roundtable --allow-publish
```

Use the ID returned by `npm trust list` for `<old-trust-id>`.
Do not revoke the old trust until the migration and the new workflow are ready.
